headline: Oil Stays Tight as Buyers Pay Up for Prompt Barrels, and Diesel Is Still the Pinch Point
paragraphs: The oil market is still tight, and the futures curve tells us that quite clearly. Brent's front month is trading about US$12.50 a barrel above the contract six months out, which means buyers are paying a big premium to get oil now rather than later. As long as shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remains disrupted, that premium is unlikely to go away quickly.

At the same time, diesel is where the real squeeze is. US distillate stocks are about 6% below their five-year average, even with refineries running at close to full capacity. Hence, refining margins are still fairly wide, although they have come off over the past month. In gas, Asia and Europe are paying almost the same price for LNG, so cargoes have little reason to favour one region over the other for now.
What should we watch? Sunday's OPEC+ meeting, any news on shipping through Hormuz, and whether US diesel stocks finally start to rebuild.

sources.title: The National: Oil set to post weekly gain as Middle East attacks stoke supply concerns
